virtual_device.title: New virtual device
virtual_device.description: A device just for its state machines, e.g. "Alice" or "House".

existing_device.title: Existing device
existing_device.description: The state machines become entities on this device, e.g. the dishwasher's smart plug or Alice's phone.

none.title: No device
none.description: A name for this group of state machines. Their entities won't be on any device.

data_description.person: Who this machine is about, e.g. Alice for "Alice day type". Just a label for now.

fallback.title: Fallback state
fallback.description: Where the machine starts, and where it goes when no rule matches.

remove_machine.title: Remove a state machine
remove_machine.description: Its entity is removed. Automations that use it stop working. To remove the last one, delete the whole entry.

placement.title: Name and device
placement.description: Moving keeps each machine's state and entity ID.

menu_options.rules: Rules: what moves the machine into each state
menu_options.settings: Name, fallback, person and flip limit

edit_states.title: States
edit_states.description: The order is the priority order. Removing the current state sends the machine to its fallback. Automations that use a removed state stop matching.

rename_state.title: Rename a state
rename_state.description: The machine keeps its place. Automations that use the old name need updating.

settings.title: Name, fallback, person and flip limit

data_description.max_flips: After this many rule-driven changes within a minute, the machine ignores its rules until the minute is up. Stops machines that read each other from flipping forever.

icons.title: State icons
icons.description: The machine's entity shows the icon of its current state.

rules.title: Rules
rules.description:
Rules belong to the state they lead to. Pick a state to see and edit its rules.

- **Trigger rules** move the machine when something happens, e.g. power drops below 3 W for 15 minutes.
- **Condition rules** keep the machine in the state while something is true. The first state from the top with a matching rule wins; when none match, the machine goes to its fallback ({fallback}).

Picking a state by hand (or a trigger rule) holds until the condition rules' answer changes.

trigger_rule.title: Trigger rule into {state}
trigger_rule.description: When any of the triggers fires, and the machine is in one of the **From** states (any, if empty), and the conditions pass, it goes to {state}.

data_description.name: Shown as the machine's reason when this rule moves it.

condition_rule.title: Condition rule for {state}
condition_rule.description: While all of these conditions are true, the machine is in {state}, unless a state above it also has a matching rule.

data_description.name: Shown as the machine's reason while this rule holds it.

loop_warning.title: These machines read each other
loop_warning.description:
With this rule, the machines form a loop: {loop}. They can keep changing each other. Each machine stops following its rules for a minute after {max_flips} rule changes in a minute (its flip limit, under Name, fallback, person and flip limit).

Save the rule anyway?

error.duplicate_state: Each state needs a different name (case doesn't count).
error.reserved_state: "unknown" and "unavailable" are Home Assistant's own states. Pick another name.
error.state_too_long: State names can be at most 255 characters.
error.duplicate_machine: Another state machine here already has that name.

calendar_event.name: Calendar has a matching event
calendar_event.description: Tests if one of the calendars has an event now, today or tomorrow, optionally only ones whose title contains some text. Unlike the calendar's own state, this sees every event, not just the next one.

when.name: When
when.description: Now: an event is going on right now. Today or tomorrow: any event on that day, all-day or not.

title_contains.name: Title contains
title_contains.description: Only events whose title contains this, e.g. PTO. Case doesn't matter. Empty: any event.

search_description.name: Also search the description
search_description.description: Match the text in the event's description too, not just its title.

event_kind.name: Kind of event
event_kind.description: All events, only all-day ones, or only ones with a start and end time.

unknown_state.message: "{state}" isn't a state of {machine}. Its states are: {states}.

set_state.name: Set state
set_state.description: Moves a state machine to a state, like picking it in the dropdown, and records why. On a machine with condition rules, it holds until their answer changes.

reason.name: Reason
reason.description: Shown in the machine's reason attribute. Defaults to "manual".

hold.name: Hold for
hold.description: On a machine with condition rules: go back to following them after this long, even if their answer hasn't changed.

clear_override.name: Clear override
clear_override.description: Stops holding a state set by hand or by a trigger rule; the machine follows its condition rules again.

flip_limit.title: {machine} is changing state too often
flip_limit.description: {machine} changed state {max_flips} times within a minute because of its rules, so it ignores them until the minute is up. Its rules may form a loop with another machine's. Check its rules, or raise its flip limit (the entry's Configure → Edit a state machine → Name, fallback, person and flip limit). This goes away after a restart or when the machine is edited.
